comparator.name: Filosofie
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme page and 2026–2027 curriculum establish a three-year, 180-ECTS Dutch-language bachelor. Years 1 and 2 each provide 60 ECTS of compulsory Philosophy and academic-skills courses. Year 3 contains a genuine 30-ECTS free-choice semester (exchange, Philosophy electives, an internal minor, or a minor at another Dutch university) and a 30-ECTS track. The generic registry target does not select a track. Filosofie Algemeen is fixed by the broad-academic-identity rule because it continues the programme’s four cross-cutting Philosophy pillars and research orientation, whereas Ondernemen is the more domain-specific practice-and-internship route. The choice was made independently of UCR fit. All 180 ECTS are accounted for without filling the genuine free-choice space.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Filosofie bachelor. Filosofie Algemeen continues the common programme’s four broad Philosophy pillars and scientific-research identity, whereas Ondernemen narrows toward an internship and applied organisational research. The route was selected before and independently of UCR course selection; the separate 30-ECTS free-choice semester remains uninstantiated.

alternatives.label: Philosophy across history, society and mind
alternatives.concept: Builds the broadest available UCR Philosophy pathway from ethics, mind, self, political philosophy, logic and persuasive reasoning, complemented by history, literature and cultural interpretation. It addresses Tilburg’s four cross-cutting pillars and Filosofie Algemeen route while remaining less philosophically specialised than the comparator.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines all five available UCR Philosophy courses with political philosophy, logic, rhetoric, historical context and interpretive humanities, so its defining feature is breadth across philosophical history, society and mind.
progression: The schedule uses six four-course semesters from Fall 2026 through Spring 2029. Personal & Professional Development is in Year 1; all course offerings match the fixed cohort terms; none of the selected courses has an unmet formal prerequisite; and eight level-3 courses are concentrated in Years 2 and 3 after introductory philosophy, politics, rhetoric, history and interpretive work.

alternatives.label: Ethics, politics, justice and institutions
alternatives.concept: Concentrates the UCR pathway on moral and political judgment, equality, freedom, justice, authority and contemporary institutions through Philosophy, Politics, Law, Sociology, History and Communication.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed route combines Ethics and Political Philosophy with law, institutions, social theory and environmental justice, making normative public questions its clearest organising focus.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces ten courses in archaeology, literary interpretation, intercultural history and general rhetoric with Law, Society & Justice, comparative politics, criminal and constitutional law, EU law, modern and contemporary sociology, environmental justice, gender history and an advanced history research seminar. The result prioritises normative public questions and institutions rather than a broad historical-philosophical survey.
progression: The schedule uses six four-course semesters with Personal & Professional Development in Year 1. Law, Society & Justice is completed in the first semester before Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, Comparative Constitutional Law and Foundations of European Union Law. All offerings match the fixed cohort terms, and eight level-3 courses occur after introductory philosophy, politics, law and sociology.

alternatives.label: Mind, language, cognition and artificial intelligence
alternatives.concept: Concentrates the UCR pathway on consciousness, mind, meaning, agency and intelligent systems by combining Philosophy with Cognitive Science, Psychology, Linguistics, Programming and AI ethics.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed route links Philosophy of Mind and questions of the self with cognitive science, psycholinguistics, psychology and AI, so mind, language and intelligent systems provide the most specific truthful label.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces twelve courses in political philosophy, law, history, archaeology, world literature and international politics with brain and behaviour, neurobiology, perception and action, psycholinguistics, social and experimental psychology, higher cognition, programming, machine learning, AI ethics and an advanced psychology research seminar. It therefore changes both the disciplinary mix and the central questions from broad philosophical history to mind, meaning and intelligent systems.
progression: The schedule uses six four-course semesters with Personal & Professional Development in Year 1. Introduction to Brain & Behavior is completed in semester 1 before Perception & Action, Psycholinguistics, Higher Order Functions and Advanced Research Seminar; introductory philosophy, rhetoric and brain science precede advanced mind, language and research work. All offerings match the fixed cohort terms, and seven level-3 courses occur in Years 2 and 3.

selection.assessment: The closest match covers Tilburg’s broad four-pillar Philosophy identity and the selected Filosofie Algemeen route. The programme’s political-social and mind-language strands each support a coherent, materially distinct UCR curriculum and are included as alternatives 2 and 3. The formal Ondernemen track is independently coherent, but the production contract permits at most three UCR alternatives; it is therefore recorded as maximum-reached.

notes.text: Tilburg supplies a continuous 150-ECTS Philosophy curriculum plus a 30-ECTS free-choice semester, including compulsory history of philosophy, epistemology, metaphysics, philosophical methodology and language, the Filosofie Algemeen track, and a required 10-ECTS thesis. UCR offers five dedicated Philosophy courses and constructs related routes with Politics, Law, Communication, History, Literature, Sociology, Cognitive Science, Psychology and AI. These interdisciplinary pathways do not reproduce Tilburg’s sustained specialist depth, full two-year compulsory sequence, dedicated third-year Philosophy track, or required Philosophy thesis.
